item.title: Sediment dynamics drive global patterns of salt-marsh vulnerability
item.dc:creator: Hangjie Lin
Sergio Fagherazzi
Cédric G. Fichot
item.description: Salt marshes protect coastlines, support biodiversity, and store substantial blue carbon, yet their rates of gain and loss vary markedly around the world. Although relative sea-level rise (RSLR) is widely recognized as a major threat, contemporary global patterns of marsh change do not simply track RSLR, suggesting additional controls mediate vulnerability. Here, we combine satellite-derived global salt-marsh change with datasets describing hydro-sedimentary regimes, human pressure, and extreme events to identify the processes underlying this spatial heterogeneity. Tidal range, suspended sediment concentration, and wave–sediment coupling are the strongest first-order predictors of contemporary marsh trajectories, outperforming RSLR in explaining global patterns. These results show that the effects of RSLR are mediated by local sediment availability, delivery, and redistribution. Building on this framework, the Salt Marsh Vulnerability Index identifies coastlines globally where physical conditions favor persistence or increase the risk of marsh degradation, providing a foundation for conservation, restoration, and blue-carbon planning. item.description: The eruption of Vesuvius volcano witnessed by Pliny the Younger in 79 CE is dated by the argon-40/argon-39 ( 40 Ar/ 39 Ar) method to 1938 ± 13 years (SD) before measurement in 2025 CE. Achievement of 0.7% precision and 0.4% accuracy at such a young age marks a precedent for 40 Ar/ 39 Ar dating and signals improved applicability of the method for constraining magma systems’ evolution, including volcanic hazard assessment. Improvements in mass spectrometry, neutron irradiation strategy, and determination of interfering neutron-induced isotopes enable this result. The data serve to determine the decay constant for the radioactive decay of potassium-40 ( 40 K) to 40 Ar that is twice as precise as the value determined by disintegration counting, thus improving the accuracy of 40 Ar/ 39 Ar dating throughout geologic time, and serves as an important datum for intercalibrating 40 Ar/ 39 Ar with other dating methods. item.description: Highly siderophile elements (HSEs) are expected to be extensively depleted in the mantle due to their affinity for metal during core formation. Yet, their abundances in the mantle far exceed the predictions based on low pressure and low temperature partitioning experiments. In addition, all HSEs are present in similar chondritic relative proportion in the mantle. This has traditionally been attributed to the late accretion of chondritic material, the late veneer. We present laser-heated diamond anvil cell experiments that quantify the partitioning behavior of five HSEs (rhenium, osmium, iridium, palladium, and gold) under pressure-temperature conditions directly relevant to early Earth’s magma ocean. Our results demonstrate a substantial decrease in metal-silicate partition coefficients with increasing temperature. Multistage accretion models reproduce the observed HSE abundances and ratios in the mantle without invoking a late veneer. This resolves the longstanding paradox of HSEs excess’ in the mantle and suggests that the delivery of volatile compounds to the young Earth is primarily explained by early accretion and differentiation processes. item.title: Model-data synthesis of benthic isotopes suggests a warmer Miocene Climatic Optimum

item.description: The Miocene Climatic Optimum (MCO, ~ 15 Ma) offers insights into warm-climate dynamics and future climate change. However, its global warmth magnitude remains uncertain due to limitations in surface and benthic proxy records. Here, we develop long-run Miocene simulations featuring deep-ocean equilibration and water isotope capability, and present a probabilistic inference framework integrating them with a global compilation of benthic foraminiferal δ ^18O to better constrain the MCO warmth. Our approach yields a maximum likelihood estimate of MCO global mean surface temperature of 7.5^∘C above preindustrial, significantly warmer than previous benthic δ ^18O-based reconstructions, implying a higher MCO-derived estimate of Earth system sensitivity. The corresponding surface temperature field shows among the best agreements with independent surface temperature proxies. This study highlights the importance of deep-ocean equilibration and proxy-model integration for accurately estimating both deep-ocean and surface temperatures, and offers a method applicable to improving global climate reconstructions across other time intervals. Combining long climate-isotope simulations with deep-sea oxygen isotope records, the Miocene Climatic Optimum (15 Ma) is estimated to have been 7.5^∘C warmer than preindustrial -- 30% above earlier estimates. item.description: Abstract The efficiency of deep carbon recycling in hot subduction systems remains debated, with contrasting models predicting either extensive shallow decarbonation or substantial carbonate retention within the subducted slab. Here we present boron-isotope and geochemical data from olivine-hosted melt inclusions in volcanic arc adakites from western Panama and in forearc high-Mg andesites from SW Japan, representing modern and Archean-like hot subduction systems. Olivine-hosted melt inclusions exhibit elevated δ 11 B values (up to +23.2‰) coupled with high Ce/Pb, La/Yb, Eu/Ti, and Th/Zr ratios, indicating melt contributions from subducted carbonate-bearing lithologies. Integration with regional CO 2 flux estimates from western Panama suggests that more than ~60% of slab carbonate escapes shallow decarbonation, likely owing to extensive forearc and arc dehydration causing substantial fluid loss, thereby suppressing fluid-mediated decarbonation beneath both the deeper forearc and arc front. These results demonstrate that substantial carbon can bypass shallow decarbonation in both modern and Archean hot subduction systems. item.title: Upscaling sediment source prediction for watershed management
item.dc:creator: Abigal Percich
Allen Gellis
James F. Fox
Admin Husic
item.description: Abstract Identifying sources of erosion is critical for effective watershed management, but existing fingerprinting methods remain resource-intensive and difficult to standardize or scale. To address this, we compiled a global synthesis of 142 sediment tracing studies across 267 watersheds and developed an explainable machine learning framework that predicts sediment provenance using remotely sensed attributes. Four sediment categories capture global erosion sources—subsurface, cultivated, non-cultivated, and infrastructure—and our model predicts their contributions with robust accuracy (R 2 = 0.40–0.53). Model interpretation confirms that predictions align with expected hydroclimatic and land cover relationships, indicating consistency with the physical processes governing sediment sourcing. When applied to six watersheds in the United States and United Kingdom, the model reveals contrasting erosional regimes: subsurface erosion dominates the Upper Mississippi and Chesapeake Bay, whereas non-cultivated surface erosion prevails across the UK watersheds. This predictive framework provides a transferable, interpretable, and data-driven tool for mapping sediment sources at large scales, enabling targeted watershed management. item.description: Abstract Temporal variations in magma plumbing influence eruption priming and the interpretation of unrest signals, yet remain poorly constrained in low-flux ocean island volcanoes. Here, we examine temporal changes in the active volcanic system beneath La Palma, Canary Islands, using clinopyroxene zoning from the 1712, 1971, and 2021 eruptions. Combining quantitative trace element mapping, thermobarometry, and cluster analysis, we show that preceding all eruptions, an evolved phonolitic crystal mush resided in the upper mantle (∼18–25 km depth) under relatively cool (1000–1025 °C) conditions. At least one week before eruption, basanitic recharge (1100–1150 °C) recycled this mush and promoted magma ascent, potentially with brief stalling in the crust (∼5–10 km). Mafic recharge was critical in unlocking the mush, yet may not represent the immediate eruption trigger. Globally, upper mantle evolved mushes may be common in ocean island basalt volcanoes, and their occurrence is likely controlled by the island evolutionary stage and magma flux. item.title: Barrier island geomorphic complexity drives storm and post-storm response
item.dc:creator: Jennifer L. Miselis
Noreen A. Buster
Daniel J. Ciarletta
Julie C. Bernier
Emily A. Wei
Rose V. Palermo
item.description: Abstract Barrier islands are at the forefront of climate-driven changes, with their resiliency threatened by rapid fluctuations in the physical drivers that shape them. Quantifying magnitudes and directions of storm-driven sediment fluxes and rates and modes of sediment recovery is essential for predicting barrier island trajectories. Yet scarce shoreface observations have limited such efforts. Here, shoreface-inclusive measurements of barrier sediment fluxes over five years following an extreme storm reveal distinct sediment redistribution patterns that vary with island geomorphology. Overwash fluxes were low compared with seaward fluxes, inlet-related landward transport, and previously modeled estimates. Without these observations, models may overestimate island elevation-building capacity that is key to sea-level adaptability. Post-storm recovery was incomplete despite human intervention, altering barrier sediment distribution from pre-storm conditions. This may increase vulnerability to future storms and rising water levels and suggests management approaches tailored to island geometry may better compete with climate change effects. item.title: Englacial authigenesis in deep Antarctic ice: implications for Martian dust oxidation
item.dc:creator: L. Lanci
B. Delmonte
M. Mattioli

item.description: Brines generated within deep ice can provide reactive micro-environments for geochemical reactions and dust aggregation, including potentially on Mars and other planetary ice environments, according to micro-scale observations from Antarctic ice cores. The discovery of englacial authigenesis has the potential to reshape our interpretation of insoluble dust records in ice cores and our understanding of planetary ice-bearing deposits on Mars. Mineralogical changes in deep ice involve iron mobilization and transformation driven by the circulation of acidic fluids within the ice matrix, leading to the authigenic formation of jarosite. Here we show that englacial authigenesis is documented across different Antarctic deep ice cores and involves the formation of mineral phases such as goethite/lepidocrocite and hematite/maghemite, in addition to jarosite. The coexistence of these phases reflects micron-scale variability in pH and water activity within the englacial brine network. Englacial authigenesis introduces biases in bulk mineralogical proxies used to reconstruct dust source conditions, and provides a grounded explanation for the anomalously high dust magnetization observed in deep Antarctic ice. We further propose that the repeated burial of dust within planetary ice reservoirs, as expected on Mars over orbital timescales, represents a viable mechanism for the oxidation, aggregation and magnetic activation of Martian airborne dust, without requiring prolonged warm and wet surface conditions. item.title: Cascading magmatic unrest and aseismic faulting in the Aegean Sea enabled by elastic stress relay
item.dc:creator: John D. Wilding
Taiyi A. Wang
Yuan-Kai Liu
Zachary E. Ross
item.description: Magma reservoirs commonly exist in clusters and situate within complex fault networks, yet sequential triggering of unrest at multiple reservoirs and faults is rarely observed. We show that the 2025 earthquake swarm in the Christiana-Santorini-Kolumbo complex of the Aegean Sea was driven by elastic stress transfer between two magma reservoirs, a 9-kilometer-long dike, and a 17-kilometer-long, southeast-dipping fault. Pressurization of the magma reservoir under Santorini triggered a dike intrusion originating from a separate magma reservoir under the Kolumbo volcano. The dike, in turn, triggered a moment magnitude ( M w ) 6.2 aseismic slip transient on a SW-NE trending branch of the Amorgos fault. Episodic bursts of upward-propagating seismicity within the geodetically constrained dike potentially indicate buoyancy-driven, segmented dike opening. We suggest that unrest in rift zones can propagate over spatial scales much larger than individual magma reservoirs and faults via sequential relay of elastic stress. item.title: Staking out the frontiers: The limits of the metazoan shallow marine fossil record
item.dc:creator: Thomas A. Neubauer
Mathias Harzhauser
item.description: The fossil record is inherently incomplete, yet its physical limits remain largely uncharted. Here, we quantify the spatiotemporal coverage of the global shallow-marine metazoan fossil record across the Phanerozoic, using a large dataset of georeferenced collections intersected with global geological data. Modeling historical sampling trajectories, we show that for most time intervals, future data accumulation is expected to be negligible, and geographic coverage is approaching saturation. For intervals with remaining potential, we reconstruct the present-day extent of unexplored but geologically accessible strata, providing spatially explicit guidance on where undetected fossil information is most likely to await discovery. Our results constitute a quantitative roadmap for prioritizing fieldwork, completing occurrence databases, and mobilizing unpublished museum collections. item.title: Magmatic origin of the Dewar magnetic anomaly: Implications for an early lunar dynamo
item.dc:creator: Xi Yang
Anna Mittelholz
Adrien Broquet
Max Moorkamp
item.description: The Moon’s ancient magnetic field provides critical insights into lunar thermal and magnetic evolution, yet the lifetime of the interior dynamo remains debated. Returned samples yield complex and contradictory paleomagnetic records, while orbital data reveal crustal magnetic anomalies of uncertain origin from either a core dynamo or transient impact-generated fields. Here, we jointly invert gravity and magnetic observations in the region around the Dewar swirl, a high-albedo feature associated with the Dewar magnetic anomaly. We identify a shallow, magnetized, high-density body consistent with buried mare basalt. Our estimates require a paleointensity exceeding 11 microtesla, suggesting an active lunar dynamo about 4.2 billion years ago, as constrained by the superposed basin ejecta. The results also show that swirl formation requires horizontal magnetization and iron oxide enrichment. These findings link a magnetic anomaly to its geologic origin and magnetizing field, providing constraints on the lunar magnetic and volcanic history. item.description: Fluctuations in the length of day (LOD) on decadal timescales are caused primarily by an exchange of angular momentum between the Earth’s mantle and core^ 1 – 3 . item.description: Ocean productivity is sensitive to climate change, and its decline in recent decades has profoundly impacted the biosphere. item.description: Abstract Marine radiocarbon archives are depleted relative to the atmosphere, which is commonly expressed as the marine radiocarbon reservoir age. item.description: Most coastal areas of the United States are sinking, with the Gulf Coast and disadvantaged communities facing the highest risk, according to an analysis of more than 190 million satellite and ground-based measurements of land elevation change. item.description: The origin of postcollisional porphyry copper deposits (PCDs) within thickened crust remains debated, particularly regarding the coupling between tectono-magmatic–volatile evolution and ore formation. Intermediate granodiorite porphyry (15.3 ± 0.1 Ma) exhibits transitional isotopic traits and rare earth element patterns, reflecting crust–mantle hybridization. Post-ore diorite porphyry (14.6 ± 0.1 Ma and 14.7 ± 0.1 Ma) displays mantle affinities, positive ∆199Hg, and enriched Sr-Nd-Hf signatures, indicating metasomatized lithospheric mantle melting. Across the sequence toward the young rocks with mantle signatures, decreasing Sr/Y ratios and increasing zircon saturation temperatures record a shift from amphibole- to plagioclase-dominated fractionation. item.description: The Xiahe-Hezuo district, located in the western Qinling orogenic belt, hosts several giant gold (Au) deposits, including the Ludousou, Zaozigou, and Jiagantan deposits arranged from north to south, which together contain > 300 t Au and significant Sb resources. However, the sources of metals and fluids, as well as the ore-forming processes responsible for the formation of these giant Au-Sb mineralizations, remain debated. This study presents integrated in-situ Pb-S-Sb isotope and bulk Hg isotope analyses of sulfides and ores from these deposits to constrain the metal sources and ore-forming processes. The Ludousou deposit, hosted in magmatic rock in the north, exhibits radiogenic Pb with 206Pb/204Pb ratios ranging from 18.04 to 19.75 and displays the most positive δ34S (mean = 3.1 ‰), δ123Sb (mean = 0.04 ‰), and δ202Hg (mean = 1.54 ‰) values. The Zaozigou deposit, hosted in both magmatic and sedimentary rocks, also shows radiogenic Pb with 206Pb/204Pb ratios between 18.44 and 20.32 and intermediate δ34S (mean = -7.3 ‰), δ123Sb (mean = -0.32 ‰), and δ202Hg (mean = 0.86 ‰) values. The Jiagantan deposit, hosted in sedimentary rock in the south, has less radiogenic Pb, with 206Pb/204Pb ratios ranging from 17.66 to 19.08, and exhibits less positive δ34S (mean = -11.6 ‰), δ123Sb (mean = -0.69 ‰), and δ202Hg (mean = -0.06 ‰) values. All Pb-S-Sb-Hg isotopic data reveal a consistent trend indicating a magmatic source with an increasing sedimentary or metamorphic contribution progressing from the Ludousou to the Zaozigou to the Jiagantan deposits, moving southward within the Xiahe-Hezuo district. The geological settings and isotopic evidence support a model in which Triassic magmatism and ore formation occurred via long-lived fluid recharge coupled with fluid-rock interaction within a network of structurally controlled fracture zones, resulting in sulfide and Au precipitation. This study underscores the critical role of fluid recharge above intrusions in the formation of giant gold deposits within magmatic-hydrothermal systems. item.description: Experimentally determined melting phase relations involving the transition from carbon dioxide-bearing anorthite to spinel peridotite at 0.5 to 1 GPa in the system CaO-MgO-Al2O3-SiO2-CO2 (CMAS-CO2) are reported. The melting reactions on each side of the transition are orthopyroxene + clinopyroxene + anorthite + vapor = forsterite + liquid, on the low-pressure side, and orthopyroxene + clinopyroxene + spinel + vapor = forsterite + liquid, on the high-pressure side. item.description: Slab-derived supercritical fluids serve as important agents for material transport in deep subduction zones. item.description: This study presents a petrological, geochemical, and geochronological investigation of a metamorphosed magmatic complex within the central segment of the Paleoproterozoic Khondalite Belt (KB) of the North China Craton (NCC). item.description: Slab subduction is the only efficient mechanism for recycling halogens from the Earth's surface into the interior, thereby regulating long-term ocean salinity and sustaining the Earth's habitability. Dehydration and melting are the two principal pathways by which subducted slabs transfer surface-derived halogens into the mantle. Previous constraints on halogen behavior in subduction zones have been broadly established on fluid-dominated arc lavas and metamorphic rocks. However, the compositions and behavior of halogens during slab melting, and their role in subduction-zone halogen cycling, remain poorly constrained. Here we present bulk-rock halogen (F and Cl), C, and S data for two Mediterranean alkaline suites formed in a subduction-related setting–leucite-bearing rocks and orogenic lamproites–interpreted to be derived from lithospheric mantle metasomatized predominantly by carbonate-rich and siliciclastic sediment melts, respectively. Both leucite-bearing rocks and high-Mg# (>75) lamproites exhibit higher F (1850–3210 and 660–4180 ppm) than N-MORB. In contrast, a subset of lamproites preserve near-primary Cl (mean ~ 389 ppm), while all leucite-bearing rocks and some of the lamproites show significant Cl depletion due to degassing. Melting models show that the mantle sources of these alkaline rocks were strongly enriched in halogens, with concentrations equivalent to ~50 times those of depleted mantle (~800 ppm F and ~ 50 ppm Cl). This suggests that substantial F and Cl can be transferred into subduction zones through sediment subduction. The mantle sources of these alkaline rocks are characterized by high F/Cl (~4.7) and by F/Nd (~20.7) and Cl/Nb (~16.8) ratios that fall within the ranges of dehydrated sediments and primary N-MORB. This contrasts sharply with dehydration-dominated arc lavas, which exhibit low F/Cl (~0.58), elevated F/Nd (~34.1), and extremely high Cl/Nb (~1315). These results indicate that sediment-melt metasomatism enriches F and Cl in the mantle source without significantly modifying F/Nd or Cl/Nb, whereas slab-fluid metasomatism preferentially enriches Cl and strongly fractionates both ratios. Our results therefore demonstrate that combined F/Cl, F/Nd, and Cl/Nb systematics provide an effective means of distinguishing the relative contributions of melting and dehydration to halogen recycling in subduction zones. item.description: The transition from magma-dominated to fluid-dominated systems marks a critical stage where metal elements combine with ligands, enabling their transport and, in some cases, the formation of economically significant mineral to ore deposits. item.dc:creator: Jabrane Labidi

item.description: The recycling of surface materials into the mantle shapes the chemical diversity of oceanic basalts. The Beni Bousera orogenic massif (Morocco) provides a unique window into these processes, exposing a great diversity of mantle pyroxenites, including samples formed from the recycling of lower oceanic crust. Here we present sulfur isotope compositions (δ34S, Δ33S, Δ36S) of graphite-free and graphite-bearing pyroxenites from Beni Bousera. In contrast, graphite-bearing pyroxenites exhibit fractionated isotopic signatures, with δ34S ~ −3.5‰, Δ33S ~ +0.065‰ and Δ36S ~ −0.45‰. Those are associated with extreme sulfur enrichment, up to 5600 ppm. Mass balance calculations indicate that these signatures reflect the addition of ~5% black shale to an igneous oceanic crust protolith. item.description: Subduction returns surface lithologies to the mantle and helps generate enriched domains sampled by ocean-island basalts (OIB). Many studies identify recycled components in OIB sources, but few resolve how these components mature into coherent, melt-fertile mantle domains. We examine this transition using Miocene and late Middle Pleistocene alkaline lavas that record temporally distinct sampling of a regional slab-modified asthenosphere above stagnant Tethyan slab material in southeastern Yunnan. New major- and trace-element, Sr–Nd–Pb and Mo isotope data for ca. 0.25–0.22 Ma Pingbian basanites are compared with published ca. 13–11 Ma Maguan basalts. Relative to Maguan, Pingbian has narrower ranges of source-sensitive trace-element ratios and Sr–Nd–Pb isotope compositions and a clearer enriched mantle 1 (EM1)-like signature, characterized by low 206Pb/204Pb and 143Nd/144Nd and intermediate 87Sr/86Sr. These features define a more focused melt-producing domain, whereas δ 98/95Mo spans −0.41‰ to +0.04‰. Integrated δ 98/95Mo–Ce/Mo, trace-element and Sr–Nd–Pb relationships are consistent with similar recycled component classes in both suites but different effective weighting, with weaker expression of eclogitized oceanic crust and sediment-derived material and stronger expression of hydrated slab mantle in Pingbian. The resolved Mo isotope excursions indicate that component-scale heterogeneity persisted within this focused source. We define OIB-source maturation as source focusing and component reweighting within an inherited recycled slab inventory, rather than replacement by a new reservoir. item.description: Subduction delivers variable sediment components to convergent margins and plays a critically important role in governing mantle oxygen fugacity (fO2), but the redox states of recycled sediments are difficult to track and remain poorly quantified. item.description: The Mingyang mafic–ultramafic complex in the Beishan Terrane has recently been discovered to host Ni-Cu sulfides that have not yet been systematically studied. This study presents olivine compositional data, zircon U-Pb geochronology, whole-rock geochemistry, and C-S-Sr-Nd isotopic systematics of the complex. The analyses aim to determine the timing of magmatism and mineralization, characterize the magma source, investigate the mechanism of sulfur saturation, and constrain the complex’s petrogenesis. The results indicate that troctolite from the complex yields a zircon U-Pb age of ca. 444 Ma. Combined with previously reported ages of 453–458 Ma, these data reveal an age span of approximately 10–14 Myr within the complex, recording two independent magmatic pulses during the Late Ordovician–Early Silurian subduction-to-collision transition: the early pulse (∼458–453 Ma) formed in an oceanic subduction volcanic arc setting, whereas the late pulse (∼444 Ma) corresponds to an initial arc-continent collision setting. The parental magmas were derived from a mixed source including asthenospheric mantle and subduction-metasomatized lithospheric mantle. The Harzburgite, orthopyroxenite, and troctolite in the complex originate from a fluid-modified enriched lithospheric mantle source, formed by 2–7 % partial melting of an amphibole-bearing garnet lherzolite with a clinopyroxene to garnet ratio of approximately 6:1. In contrast, gabbro and gabbro-diorite at the complex are derived from a fluid-modified transitional lithospheric mantle source, generated by ≤ 10 % partial melting of an amphibole-bearing spinel lherzolite. Assimilation of upper crustal material by the mantle-derived magma, which added external sulfur, was the key in achieving sulfur saturation of the parental magma, with an assimilation degree estimated at 20–30 %. Integrated analysis of the complex’s structure, lithology, geochemistry, olivine composition, and alteration features suggests that the harzburgite and orthopyroxenite within the complex have a high potential for Ni, Cu, and Co mineralization. The Mingyang complex represents a Late Ordovician (ca. 460–440 Ma) Ni-Cu mineralization event in the Beishan area, distinct from the main Permian mineralization epoch. This study preliminarily constrains the formation age and petrogenesis of the complex, contributing not only to a deeper understanding of the metallogenesis of magmatic Ni-Cu sulfide deposits, but alsoproviding a theoretical basis for the discovery of other Ni and Cu occurrences. item.description: The Bou Azzer–El Graara inlier records the transition from the Pan-African major collisional phase to the WACadomian transpressive phase of deformation, marked by ca. 650 Ma syn-collisional intrusions (e.g. Ait Ahmane) and the ~540 Ma post-collisional Bleida intrusion. Field investigations also reveal the presence of pegmatitic–aplitic dikes marking a magmatic–hydrothermal transition. The disseminated hypogene copper mineralization; along with potassic, phyllic, and propylitic alteration assemblages, are characteristic evidence of porphyry copper systems. While local geological factors influence mineralization and preservation, the fundamental controls on ore genesis are linked to large-scale geodynamic and plate-tectonic processes. In this case, the Bou Azzer–El Graara inlier exhibits an overprinting of magmatic, and hydrothermal events by tectonic processes that have partially obscured some field characteristics typically associated with porphyry systems. For these reasons, whole-rock and radiogenic-isotope geochemistry are used to aid in enhancing the overall interpretation, following the recent approaches of previous studies. The syn-collisional Cryogenian granitoids record an emplacement in a compressive regime linked to obduction and fore-arc closure, and display clear signatures of magma fertility conditions: major-element contents by SiO2 ≥60 wt%, Al2O3 ≥15 wt%, MgO-poor, low Y and Yb, and enriched in LILE (positive Rb and Ba anomalies). Trace-element ratios (e.g. Sr/Y, Dy/Yb, V/Sc) further support porphyry Cu fertility. These features suggest that the Bou Azzer–El Graara intrusions formed from a fertile parental magmatic system capable of generating Pan-African syn-collisional porphyry copper deposits (PCD) (ca. 647 Ma). item.title: Grain- to outcrop-scale transport and mineralization of CO2 and rare earth elements in a mélange vein system, northeastern Connecticut, United States
item.dc:creator: Anne A. Haws

item.description: Metamorphic fluid-rock interactions make key contributions to the global carbon cycle and can transport and deposit critical elements, so it is necessary to examine these interactions quantitatively. This work focused on a network of amphibolite-facies carbonate-silicate veins in mélange in northeastern Connecticut, United States, which provides evidence for CO2 infiltration and mineralization in mélange blocks. Pseudosection modeling of mineral assemblages in veins and altered selvages indicates that they formed from a fluid with high XCO2, ~0.8, which was introduced to the mélange blocks primarily by fracturing. Infiltration of CO2 and growth of carbonate minerals in selvages were facilitated by migration along grain boundaries and mineral dissolution-reprecipitation reactions. Mass balance calculations reveal that veins and selvages underwent considerable volatile gains (+1100% on average) due to carbonate mineralization and sequestered ~580 kg CO2 per cubic meter of altered rock, indicating that they were efficient CO2 traps. Because fluids were largely channelized in veins, however, carbonated veins and selvages make up ~10% of the blocks by volume, decreasing overall carbonation efficiency. Results also indicate that heavy rare earth elements (HREEs) were mobilized during fluid-rock interaction but trapped by garnet growth in veins and selvages. We therefore suggest that garnet may trap HREEs in metamorphic systems and affect their availability for ore-forming processes. Our calculations also reveal that some elemental mass changes were large at the local level, but values were near zero for most elements when all vein-selvage systems were averaged, suggesting that these elements were primarily cycled within the vein system. Thus, individual vein-selvage systems are not necessarily representative of processes in the vein system overall. item.description: Hydrothermal overprinting is generally common for carbonatite-hosted rare earth element (REE) deposit, yet the specific mineralization mechanisms driven by hydrothermal fluids remain unclear. In situ LA-ICP-MS U–Pb dating of fluorapatite from the two carbonatite types yield lower intercept ages of 150.0 ± 7.1 Ma and 128.4 ± 6.5 Ma, coinciding with the Late Jurassic to Early Cretaceous granitic magmatism in the region. Fluorapatite grains from both carbonatite types exhibit zoning or turbid textures, which are distinct from typical magmatic apatite. They show elevated Na and REE contents, while concentrations in Si, Mg and Mn are low. The low (La/Yb)CN, (La/Lu)CN, (La/Sm)CN, and Sr/Y ratios further support a secondary hydrothermal origin. The occurrence of silicate minerals, together with partial dissolution–reprecipitation textures in fluorapatite and monazite suggest a certain contribution from Late Mesozoic hydrothermal overprints associated with granite intrusions. In contrast, the fluorapatite 87Sr/86Sr ratios (0.7047–0.7050) overlap those of the host carbonatite system, indicating that Sr was predominantly sourced from carbonatite-derived fluids. The dissolution–reprecipitation of fluorapatite and monazite facilitated the crystallization of secondary REE-rich mineral phases. These results highlight the significant metallogenic potential of carbonatite systems in orogenic settings that have undergone multiple episodes of tectono-hydrothermal reactivation, and provide important insights into the mechanisms of REE remobilization and economic mineralization. item.description: The southeastern coastal metallogenic belt of China is one of the country’s most important fluorite-producing regions. Fluorite mineralization in this region has generally been considered to be concentrated in the Late Cretaceous, but recent direct dating results suggest that its metallogenic history may involve multiple hydrothermal episodes. The temporal and genetic relationships between fluorite mineralization and widespread Early Cretaceous volcanic–intrusive magmatism therefore remain unclear. This study investigates the Niueling fluorite deposit in central Zhejiang Province using field observations, zircon U–Pb geochronology, direct fluorite U–Pb dating, fluid inclusion microthermometry, Raman spectroscopy, REE geochemistry, and H–O–Sr–Nd isotopic analyses to constrain the timing, fluid evolution, and material sources of fluorite mineralization. Zircon U–Pb dating shows that the granite porphyry was emplaced at 134.3 ± 1.1 Ma, whereas fluorite veins locally cut the porphyry. Direct fluorite U–Pb dating yielded corrected ages of 62.4 ± 4.6 Ma and 62.7 ± 5.6 Ma, demonstrating that fluorite mineralization occurred during the Paleogene rather than during Early Cretaceous magmatism. The apparent ca. 190 Ma fluorite Sm–Nd regression age is interpreted as a mixing line produced by multi-stage hydrothermal activity and open-system behavior. Fluid inclusions indicate low- to intermediate-temperature, mostly low-salinity NaCl–H2O ± CO2 (±CH4) fluids, with estimated trapping pressures of 6.02–22.72 MPa and mineralization depths of approximately 0.20–0.76 km. H–O isotopes indicate a dominant contribution from deeply circulating meteoric water, whereas REE and Sr–Nd isotopes suggest that F was mainly sourced from pre-existing F-bearing granite porphyry, volcanic–subvolcanic host rocks, and basement-related lithologies, whereas Ca was likely supplied by dissolution and alteration of Ca-bearing minerals during water–rock interaction. The Niueling deposit therefore records decoupling between the fluid medium and ore-forming material sources. We interpret it as a structurally controlled, low- to intermediate-temperature meteoric-hydrothermal vein-type fluorite deposit formed during Paleogene tectonic reactivation, with limited direct magmatic fluid input. These results provide new evidence for Paleogene fluorite mineralization in central Zhejiang and highlight the temporal and genetic diversity of fluorite mineralization in South China. item.description: Whether Earth’s earliest continental nuclei formed in subduction-related (plate tectonics) or thick, plateau-like (not related to plate tectonics) regimes remains controversial. Resolving this debate hinges on elucidating the petrogenesis of the earliest tonalite-trondhjemite-granodiorite (TTG) suites, specifically the nature of their basaltic sources and physico-chemical conditions (pressure-temperature) during partial melting. Here, we investigated the Paleoarchean Steynsdorp Complex—the oldest TTG complex in South Africa’s Barberton granitoid-greenstone terrane (BGGT). Zircon U-Pb dating confirms the main magmatic phase at ca. 3.51 Ga and identifies a previously unrecognized ca. 3.22 Ga magmatic episode within the same complex. Thermodynamic modeling indicates that both the TTG phases were derived from partial melting of hydrous basaltic sources but at distinct pressures: 1.1–1.3 GPa for the ca. 3.51 Ga phase and 0.9–1.1 GPa for the ca. 3.22 Ga phase. Isotopically, the ca. 3.51 Ga TTGs yield mantle-like δ18O and εHf(t) values tracking a ca. 3.7–3.55 Ga source and reflecting melting within a thickened mafic plateau. In contrast, the ca. 3.22 Ga TTGs exhibit a distinct decoupled isotopic signature characterized by elevated δ18O (up to 7.0‰) and highly positive εHf(t) values (up to +5). Combined with elevated Mg# and Cr concentrations, these geochemical characteristics indicate that the ca. 3.22 Ga magmatism resulted from subduction-driven tectonic thickening followed by lower crustal delamination, which induced asthenospheric upwelling and subsequent hybridization of juvenile mantle-derived melts with supracrustal-derived melts. Our results suggest a fundamental transition from stable plateau growth at ca. 3.51 Ga to a dynamic subduction-delamination regime at ca. 3.22 Ga, which may ultimately drive the formation and stabilization of the BGGT continental nuclei. item.description: The production and differentiation of felsic magmas are one of the key features of continental crust on Earth. Understanding the processes and mechanisms of highly differentiated magmas is crucial for unraveling lithospheric architecture and deep Earth processes, deciphering the evolution of transcrustal magmatic systems, and exploring the metallogenesis of critical metals. Granitic rocks widely occur in China, where their precursor magmas exhibit particularly pronounced differentiation. The highly differentiated granites are common in South China, the Himalaya, Xinjiang (Central Asia), and the Great Xing’an Range. They exhibit diverse characteristics, complex geological settings and significant mineralization potential, thus requiring further investigation. We suggest that such petrogenetic and metallogenic diversities are governed by multiple factors, including source compositions, tectonic setting, and heat and volatile supply. item.description: Abstract Oceanic lithosphere is continuously destroyed by subduction, challenging our ability to develop tectonic reconstructions. item.title: A comparative study on the occurrence and enrichment mechanisms of Co and Ni in different types of marine polymetallic nodules and cobalt-rich Fe–Mn crusts: Implications for seafloor Co and Ni mineralization
item.dc:creator: Sucheng Huang

item.description: Marine ferromanganese crusts and nodules are valuable deep-sea mineral resources that host critical metals such as cobalt and nickel, which are indispensable for advanced and environmentally sustainable technologies. This study systematically investigates the characteristics, occurrence and enrichment mechanisms of Co and Ni in hydrogenetic, hydrogenetic-diagenetic, and phosphatized FeMn deposits from the Pacific, using a combination of sequential leaching and microscopic to nanoscale mineralogical analyses. Results show that Co and Ni are predominantly hosted in Mn-oxide minerals, particularly vernadite and todorokite. Cobalt is enriched in vernadite under hydrogenetic conditions, whereas Ni is incorporated into the tunnel structure of todorokite during suboxic diagenesis. Hydrogenetic deposits exhibit high Co and moderate Ni, with Co structurally bound to vernadite via oxidative substitution and Ni adsorbed and incorporated into the vernadite lattice. Hydrogenetic-diagenetic nodules exhibit alternating Co-rich vernadite and Ni-rich todorokite layers, reflecting pore water-mediated diagenesis where Mg2+ assists interlayer expansion of vernadite and todorokite crystallization. Phosphatization triggers substantial remobilization: the contents of Co decreases by 23.6% due to reductive dissolution, while Ni increases by 87.5% through recrystallization into diagenetic todorokite and associated transitional 10 Å Mn-oxides. The extent of phosphatization governs Ni redistribution, with low-intensity causing Ni loss and higher intensities promoting Ni enrichment. These findings support a coherent enrichment pathway from hydrogenetic vernadite to diagenetic todorokite, emphasizing control by redox conditions and mineralogical transformation. This study advances understanding of marine metal cycling and provides a predictive framework for exploration of critical metals in deep-sea FeMn deposits. item.description: Boron concentrations and isotopic compositions were determined in basaltic glasses from the Eastern Romanche Ridge Transform Intersection along the Equatorial Mid-Atlantic Ridge, a tectonically and thermally complex ridge–transform setting characterised by reduced magma supply and consequently limited melt homogenisation. These relationships link contrasting volatile inventories to mantle components independently defined by trace-element and radiogenic-isotope systematics. item.description: Accurate characterization of hydrothermal alteration zones is critical for ore targeting within porphyry-epithermal systems. Although short-wave infrared (SWIR) spectroscopy is effective for identifying hydrous alteration minerals, it fails to detect crucial anhydrous phases, such as K-feldspar within potassic zones. Magnetic susceptibility measurements offer a solution to this constraint as magnetite mostly precipitates during potassic alteration but can be destroyed during later alteration (e.g., phyllic, sericite-chlorite, and propylitic). Consequently, this study integrates SWIR spectroscopy with magnetic susceptibility data to reconstruct the alteration architecture of the Eastern Au deposit in the Songshu’nangou district, North Qilian orogenic belt. Chlorite, white mica, and other minerals were identified in ∼48%, ∼44%, and ∼5% of the analyzed samples from the Eastern Au deposit, respectively, where the abundant white mica shows a spatial association with the Au mineralization, reflected by crystallinity (SWIR-IC > 1.7) and wAlOH (Pos2200 > 2200 nm) values. The magnetic susceptibility (K bulk) values are highest in potassic alteration zones and lowest in phyllic alteration zones. Combined SWIR and magnetic susceptibility data delineate a previously unrecognized vertical alteration zonation with a deep potassic (average K bulk = 7.679 × 10−3 SI units) zone transitioning upwards and outwards into propylitic, sericite-chlorite (strong and weak), and local phyllic alteration zones. This zonation, coupled with the relatively high K bulk values, spatially associated with the Au mineralization in the deep potassic alteration zone, provides compelling evidence for the presence of an underlying porphyry Au system beneath the known intermediate-sulfidation (IS) epithermal mineralization, indicating that the Eastern Au deposit likely represents a porphyry-epithermal Au system. Our results demonstrate that combined SWIR-IC and wAlOH values of white micas may serve as potential vectors in epithermal systems with magnetic susceptibility being a reliable vector for targeting deeper porphyry Au mineralization within potassic alteration zones. The identification of potassic alteration at depth reveals the exploration potential of the Eastern Au deposit, and provides useful guidance for exploring similar porphyry-epithermal Au systems in the North Qilian orogenic belt.
